title: In This World Clocks Stop For People Who Are Waiting
description: Every clock in Mr. Hayashi's shop stopped forty years ago, and so did one clock in Nanami's own kitchen. Who would your clock be waiting for? #anime #shorts #animestory #retroanime

characters.Nanami: 12-year-old Japanese girl, long black hair in two low pigtails, big brown eyes, white sailor school uniform with navy collar and red ribbon, navy pleated skirt, white socks, brown loafers, small silver wristwatch, no hat
characters.Dad: 42-year-old Japanese fisherman, short black hair, tanned face, orange rubber fishing overalls over a grey t-shirt, white towel around his neck, black rubber boots, no hat
characters.Mr. Hayashi: 68-year-old Japanese man, neat white hair combed back, thin white mustache, round gold-rimmed glasses, white shirt with sleeves rolled up, brown leather work apron, grey trousers, no hat
characters.Grandma Tomoe: 67-year-old Japanese woman, grey hair in a neat bun, gentle face, dusty pink cardigan over a white blouse, long navy skirt, white apron, no glasses, no hat

scenes.say: In this world, clocks stop for people who are waiting. Nanami's watch freezes every evening until her dad's fishing boat comes home. Then it ticks again.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Medium shot on a quiet 1990s Japanese fishing harbor pier at sunset, Nanami sitting on the wooden edge, holding up her wrist and frowning at her small silver watch. [4-7s] Close-up of the small silver wristwatch on Nanami's wrist, its second hand frozen. [7-10s] Medium shot on the harbor pier as Dad steps off a small white fishing boat and Nanami runs to hug him, her watch hand ticking again.

scenes.say: But one shop in town never ticks. Old Mr. Hayashi's repair shop has forty clocks on the wall, and every single one stopped at ten past four, forty years ago.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Medium shot inside a small dusty clock repair shop on a seaside town street, Nanami stepping through the door, staring at a wall covered in old wooden clocks. [4-7s] Close-up inside the clock repair shop of several old wooden wall clocks, every pendulum hanging perfectly still. [7-10s] Medium shot inside the clock repair shop of Mr. Hayashi at his workbench, bent over a pocket watch with tweezers, warm lamp light.

scenes.say: So Nanami asks who he's waiting for. He shrugs. A girl who promised to meet him at the bus stop. She never came. He just keeps fixing everyone else's clocks.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Medium shot inside the clock repair shop of Nanami leaning on the workbench, asking, while Mr. Hayashi keeps working. [4-7s] Close-up inside the clock repair shop of Mr. Hayashi pausing, looking over his gold-rimmed glasses with a sad small smile. [7-10s] Medium shot inside the clock repair shop of Mr. Hayashi handing a fixed clock to Nanami, the still wall of clocks behind him.

scenes.say: That night, Nanami looks up at Grandma's kitchen clock. It's been broken her whole life. Its hands point at ten past four. Grandma says she just never got it fixed.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Medium shot inside a small 1990s Japanese family kitchen at night, Nanami at the low table freezing with chopsticks in her hand, looking up at the wall. [4-7s] Close-up of an old round wooden kitchen wall clock above the stove, its hands frozen at ten past four. [7-10s] Medium shot inside the kitchen of Grandma Tomoe at the sink, waving a hand, avoiding Nanami's eyes.

scenes.say: Nanami asks one question. Grandma goes pale. Forty years ago, she waited at the bus stop until dark. He never came. She was on the wrong side of the road.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Close-up inside the family kitchen of Grandma Tomoe's face as she turns, a dish slipping still in her hands. [4-7s] Medium shot of a young woman in a 1950s style pink dress waiting alone at a small wooden country bus shelter at dusk. [7-10s] Wide shot of a quiet country road at dusk with two small wooden bus shelters facing each other, one young man waiting on the far side, neither seeing the other.

scenes.say: Next morning, Nanami walks Grandma into the repair shop. Mr. Hayashi drops his screwdriver. Forty clocks start ticking at once. In this world, clocks stop for people who are waiting.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Medium shot at the door of the small clock repair shop as Nanami leads Grandma Tomoe inside by the hand. [4-7s] Close-up inside the clock repair shop of Mr. Hayashi's face, his screwdriver falling from his fingers, eyes filling with tears. [7-10s] Medium shot inside the clock repair shop of Grandma Tomoe and Mr. Hayashi facing each other in silence, every pendulum on the wall behind them swinging again, Nanami smiling at the door.
